titre: Dune Director Admits He’s ‘Deeply Disappointed’ by Showdown With Avengers: Doomsday
chapo: Dune: Part 3 faces a box-office showdown with Avengers: Doomsday after Disney scheduled its Marvel blockbuster for Dec. 18.
extrait: The two blockbuster franchises are heading for a massive box-office showdown Denis Villeneuve isn't thrilled about having to share a release date with Marvel's next Avengers movie. The Dune: Part Three director has admitted he's "deeply disappointed" after Disney scheduled Avengers: Doomsday for the same December release date as his upcoming sci-fi sequel. In an interview with Time, Villeneuve discussed the unusual box-office showdown between the two highly anticipated films, both of which are scheduled to open Dec. 18. "The first Dune came out at the end of the pandemic. We made a great box office in a very rough environment. But we had the winds against us," Villeneuve told Time, pointing to the challenges surrounding the first two installments. Dune: Part Two was originally expected to arrive in the fall before being pushed to the end of winter because of the Hollywood strikes. Villeneuve said he had hoped the third movie would finally enjoy a more straightforward theatrical release, without a pandemic or industry shutdown complicating its prospects. Instead, Marvel's biggest franchise is now going head-to-head with his film. "So I was deeply disappointed," he said. "But we had committed to this date, to IMAX. It was impossible to move. So I accepted my fate, praying to the gods of cinema." Villeneuve acknowledged that Dune doesn't have the same commercial muscle as the Marvel Cinematic Universe, describing Avengers as a "T. rex" and his franchise as a "sexy little animal that has a lot of firepower." Villeneuve's first two Dune films made $411 million and $715 million at the worldwide box office, while Marvel's Avengers movies have consistently grossed in the billions. "I'm no fool. Those movies are a mammoth," he said, adding that he hopes Dune: Part Three will survive the box-office competition. Still, the filmmaker isn't necessarily viewing the simultaneous releases as a straightforward rivalry. He suggested the two movies could combine to create one of the biggest box-office weekends of all time. "Am I in competition with the Avengers? Absolutely not," Villeneuve told Time. "But I stand proud because I think the film delivers." Dune: Part Three will adapt elements of Frank Herbert's Dune Messiah, picking up years after the events of Dune: Part Two. Timothée Chalamet returns as Paul Atreides, alongside Zendaya, Florence Pugh, and other familiar faces. titre: Denis Villeneuve Was 'Deeply Disappointed' by Disney's Decision to Release Avengers: Doomsday on the Same Day as Dune: Part Three
chapo: Denis Villeneuve has revealed his disappointment at Disney's decision to release Avengers: Doomsday in theaters on the same day as Dune: Part Three.
extrait: Denis Villeneuve has revealed his disappointment at Disney's decision to release Avengers: Doomsday in theaters on the same day as Dune: Part Three. Doomsday was initially due out on May 1 this year, but was delayed to December 18 — a date Dune 3 had already claimed. Because of the clash, Avengers: Doomsday misses out on an Imax release, with Villeneuve’s trilogy-ender having already snapped up exclusivity for the big screens. In a new interview with Time, Villeneuve ran through the various release challenges the Dune movies have endured, and said he thought that with Part Three, he’d finally have a clear run of it. “Listen, I will be honest,” he began. “The first Dune came out at the end of the pandemic. We made a great box office in a very rough environment. But we had the winds against us. Then the second movie, same thing. We were meant to release in the fall, and we had to release at the end of winter because of the two Hollywood strikes. We had success, but it was not easy. The third time, I said to myself, ‘Finally, there is no pandemic, no strike in sight. We will have a normal release.’ Then Disney put the biggest franchise of all time against us. I’m no fool. Those movies are a mammoth. “So I was deeply disappointed. But we had committed to this date, to Imax. It was impossible to move. So I accepted my fate, praying to the gods of cinema. Dune is not a mammoth like the Avengers, but it’s a sexy little animal that has a lot of firepower, and I hope we will survive. It could be one of the biggest box-office weekends of all time because of both movies. Am I in competition with the Avengers? Absolutely not. It’s a T. rex. But I stand proud because I think the film delivers.” Avengers: Doomsday is expected to be one of the biggest movies of all time, with a box office haul Disney will hope matches up to previous Avengers films. It’s thought December 18 could be the largest box office weekend ever, when you factor in Dune 3’s launch. Fans have dubbed the dual release ‘DunesDay,’ in a sort of sci-fi heavy follow-up to 'Barbenheimer.' But will Dune 3 benefit from Avengers: Doomsday’s release or suffer from it? Villeneuve is putting a brave face on the situation here — I wouldn’t be surprised if there’s plenty of worry internally. According to the New York Times, Legendary Entertainment and Warner Bros. spent an estimated $200 million to make Dune 3, excluding marketing.
